messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] streaming.p99 > 4s in eu-west-2; auto-created incident. please ack if oncall.
maya (oncall): acking. seeing p95 -> ~1.0s, p99 ~4.2s starting ~09:07 UTC. alerts for streaming stalls and increased retry rates.
sara (sre): sampled proxy logs show long TLS handshake durations and repeated SYN retransmits to upstream model nodes. also some DNS lookup timeouts clustered during spike.
tom (net-eng): pulling VPC/NAT telemetry: one NAT gateway (nat-eu2b-07) has high `AllocatedPorts` usage and `PortAllocationErrors` spikes. inter-AZ egress counters show a surge from eu-west-2a to eu-west-2b paths.
ben (infra): on a proxy node: `ss -s` and `ss -tan | grep TIME_WAIT | wc -l` -> ~72k TIME_WAIT; conntrack entries ~118k on the host. ephemeral port exhaustion symptoms likely.
sara (sre): sample logs:```
2026-03-15T09:08:52Z proxy-21 stream=xzy tls_syn_retransmit=3 tls_handshake_ms=4120 dns_lookup_ms=180 upstream_ip=10.0.45.7 stall=1
2026-03-15T09:08:53Z proxy-22 stream=xzz tls_handshake_ms=3980 upstream_connect_ms=70 retry=1
```
lina (support): customers reporting progressive streaming stalls and reconnects, enterprise contact queue filling up. pulling list of affected accounts now.
carol (product): need ETA for mitigation and a short customer blurb. also capture which customers impacted and whether any SLA limits hit.
maya (oncall): quick impact calc: ~2.9% of active streams saw >=1 stall >2s; reconnects per minute up 4.1x. not total outage but user-visible degradation for a subset.
tom (net-eng): route history shows a transient flapping of a transit route at ~09:05 which made egress prefer NAT in eu-west-2b. combined with increased short-lived upstream connections -> concentrated NAT port usage. also seeing increased packet retransmits on AZb<->AZc.
ben (infra): AWS NAT logs confirm port allocation failures around 09:06-09:14. if many clients open new TLS sessions per request, the ephemeral port pool dries out quickly.
sara (sre): mitigation options ranked: (1) revert egress to AZ-local NATs (fast) (2) enable proxy upstream connection reuse / keepalive (fast canary) (3) add additional NAT capacity / launch NAT instances (slower) (4) emergency per-pod ENI routing for critical customers (manual, higher risk).
maya (oncall): what's lowest-risk immediate fix?
tom (net-eng): route bias to AZ-local NATs is the fastest: update route table to prefer local NAT gateway for each AZ. I can push change in ~3 minutes. will also apply BGP dampening on the transit peer to stop further flaps.
ben (infra): preparing `aws ec2 replace-route` commands for the cluster route tables; will rotate egress back to nat-eu2a-local / nat-eu2b-local per-AZ. staging test passed.
sara (sre): prepping a canary deploy to enable keepalives/reuse in model-proxy: will roll to 5% initially. command: `kubectl -n infra patch ds/model-proxy -p '{"spec": {"template": {"spec": {"containers": [{"name":"proxy","env":[{"name":"UPSTREAM_KEEPALIVE","value":"true"}]}]}}}}'`
lina (support): drafting interim customer note: "We're investigating elevated streaming latency in EU. Engineers are applying network routing and proxy fixes; we'll update with progress."
ben (infra): executing route replace for eu-west-2a route table to nat-eu2a-local at 09:15:40 UTC. then eu-west-2b will be similarly adjusted.
ben (infra): route updates applied. monitoring NAT metrics and conntrack.
tom (net-eng): applied BGP dampening to transit peer to reduce update churn; BGP flaps down.
sara (sre): keepalive canary rolled at 09:18:12 UTC to 5% of proxy nodes. initial telemetry shows upstream connection reuse rate climb and new TLS sessions drop.
maya (oncall): 09:22 metrics: streaming.p95 down to ~210ms, p99 dropping from 4.2s -> 750ms. NAT port allocation errors trending to zero. TIME_WAIT and conntrack counts falling. :white_check_mark:
lina (support): sent an update to affected customers noting improvement and root cause being investigated.
carol (product): please preserve timeline and affected-customer list for postmortem. prioritize enterprise customers for outreach.
tom (net-eng): preliminary RCA: transient routing flaps caused cross-AZ egress concentration through a single NAT gw, which exhausted ephemeral ports and produced TLS handshake retries and DNS backoffs, manifesting as streaming tail stalls. contributing factor: proxy default behavior of opening short-lived TLS connections per request.
sara (sre): follow-ups / action items: - enforce AZ-local egress preference in infra templates and add automated rebalancer - default enable upstream connection pooling / keepalive in model-proxy - alert on NAT port exhaustion and high TIME_WAIT/conntrack ratios - review transit peer BGP config and dampening thresholds
ben (infra): starting work to add automated detection + remediation for egress imbalance; will also document runbook steps for emergency ENI-based egress if needed.
maya (oncall): filing incident INC-2026-0115 and assigning tom (net-eng) for BGP/routing, ben (infra) for automation, sara (sre) for proxy changes, and maya for customer comms/follow-up.
carol (product): include a dedicated customer-facing postmortem (timeline, impact, mitigations, ETA for fixes). Lina will coordinate.
lina (support): will prepare draft postmortem and customer notification.
maya (oncall): handing off monitoring to night team at 10:05UTC. runbook: monitor streaming.p99, nat.PortAllocationErrors, proxy.upstream_reuse_rate.
incident-bot: incident status -> mitigated; severity -> monitoring.
